chunks: And that which Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqī narrated from Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Jaʿfarī, who said:

When I departed from Minā, I intended to stay in Makkah, so I completed the salat. Then news came to me from home, and I found that I had no choice but to go back home. I did not know whether I should complete or shorten [the prayer], and Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام was at that time in Makkah, so I went to him and related the story to him.
So he said to me: “Return to shortening [the prayer].”

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: the kunyah of the Imam عليه السلام addressed in this report
key_terms.أُقَصِّرُ: to shorten the prayer as prescribed for a traveler
key_terms.التَّقْصِيرِ: shortening the prayer in the state of travel
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the ritual prayer whose ruling here concerns completion or shortening during travel
key_terms.الْمُقَامَ: residing or staying in a place with the intention of remaining there
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the well-known location associated with the rites of hajj

ai.seo_question: If I intended to stay in Makkah and complete my prayers, then had to travel back home, should I shorten my salat again?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for a traveler whose intention changed after deciding to reside in Makkah and complete the salat. Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام instructed him to return to shortening the prayer, indicating the legal effect of resuming travel rather than residence.
